aktion.finding_paraphrase: German Aktion continues Latin actio; finite compound component must be separately segmented.

aktie.finding_paraphrase: Aktie comes via Dutch actie from Latin actio; Aktien is the plural.

atom.finding_paraphrase: Atom comes through Latin atomus from Greek atomos; the complete modern base is Atom.

atombombe.finding_paraphrase: Atombombe is the nuclear explosive noun; finite Atom+Bombe component analysis is explicit.

anis_de.finding_paraphrase: German botanical Anis continues Middle High German anis and Latin anisum.

system_en.finding_paraphrase: English system continues Late Latin systema and Greek systema; no new token-frequency partition follows.

anise.finding_paraphrase: English anise is the aromatic plant or its seed, rather than scientific unequal anis-.

system_es.finding_paraphrase: Spanish sistema continues Late Latin systema and Greek systema.

sistematizar.finding_paraphrase: RAE identifies derivation from systema with -izar, supporting this exact derivational head.

anis_es.finding_paraphrase: Spanish anis comes through French anis from Latin anisum and Greek; botanical and liqueur readings share the lexical base.

system_fr.finding_paraphrase: French systeme continues Greek sustema; this is a lexical-base relation rather than translated gloss.

anis_fr.finding_paraphrase: French anis comes through Latin anisum from Greek anison and names aromatic plants.

anice.finding_paraphrase: Italian anice comes from Greek anison and Latin anisum; plant and aromatic-product readings retain the base.

sistema_it.finding_paraphrase: Italian noun sistema continues Latin systema; verb aggregate needs the separately established common component policy.

verwalter.finding_paraphrase: Verwalter is derived from verwalten; personnel-management compound does not establish an alter component.

alter.finding_paraphrase: English alter is from Latin alterare, derived from alter other; it does not license German Verwalter or the age noun Alter.

age.finding_paraphrase: German Alter is the age noun from Middle High German alter and Old High German altar.

osservare.finding_paraphrase: Italian osservare continues Latin observare, independently supporting the finite national observ~osserv correspondence.

attimo.finding_paraphrase: Attimo is a popular variant of atomo; documented history alone does not approve recognizable modern atom in this form.

actin.finding_paraphrase: Protein actin has probable act or activate ancestry; Greek ray actin- is a separate combining form.

lieutenant.finding_paraphrase: Lieutenant has the lieu/tenant history, but lacks the complete loc component required here.

naive.finding_paraphrase: Naive has native/nativus ancestry but does not retain the complete recognizable nat component.

atomic.finding_paraphrase: Atomic denotes relations to atoms, nuclear activity, atomism or minute size; the finite atom+ic component is supported.

atomar.finding_paraphrase: Atomar describes atoms or nuclear matters, supporting the exact Atom+ar derivational component.
